HQIDS.focus: Joint picture, early warning and the two-chokepoint plan

NAVY.focus: SAR-verified picture, dark-vessel flags, escorts and ISR by risk

ISRO.name: ISRO · satellite tasking
ISRO.focus: Where to point SAR passes before the imagery is needed

DIA.name: Defence Intelligence Agency
DIA.focus: Behavioural warning: shipping moves before strikes do

MOPNG.name: MoPNG and ISPRL · energy security
MOPNG.focus: SPR cover, crude substitution, LPG and LNG exposure

MEA.name: Ministry of External Affairs
MEA.focus: Diplomatic track for passage, supplier deals and the Red Sea route

DGS.name: DG Shipping · Indian-flag merchant fleet
DGS.focus: Advisories, GNSS-interference reporting and NavIC for Gulf traders

R1: Fuse SAR detections with AIS at IFC-IOR; auto-flag dark vessels of 80 m and over near chokepoints
R2: Four behavioural indicators: transits, dark rate, war-risk premium, GNSS interference
R3: Allocate by the Threat-Opacity Index, refreshed monthly; add Bab el-Mandeb to SAR tasking
R4: At least 82% crude-substitution capability; LPG reserve of 30 days or more; SPR Phase-II
R5: Joint plan for Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb closing together; bypass pipelines exit via the Red Sea
R6: NavIC-capable receivers and GNSS-interference reporting for Indian-flag Gulf traders

HQIDS: Adopt this dashboard as the weekly chokepoint brief; plan on S3 while the data track it (RMSE 0.6 vs 15.7 for S1).
Activate the two-chokepoint plan: Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb both contested for most of 2027.
Shift from closure to managed-passage posture (S2): escort windows, not escort convoys.
NAVY: Flag every dark vessel of 80 m+ within 100 km of a chokepoint; task ISR to the three Gulf dark anchorages.
Sustain Op Urja Suraksha-type escorts through 2027; refresh the Threat-Opacity ranking monthly.
Keep SAR-AIS fusion running: dark rates are the first sign of a relapse.
ISRO: Task SAR passes to the very-high-risk cells the model flags, before imagery is requested.
Add Bab el-Mandeb and the Gulf of Aden to standing SAR tasking.
Share detections with IFC-IOR within the pass window, not days later.
DIA: Watch the four behavioural indicators weekly; strike counts alone gave no warning in Feb 2026.
A 30% fall in Hormuz traffic over 8 weeks, as in Nov 2025, with rising dark rates.
Monitor for relapse: dark rate rising while transits recover.
MOPNG: Plan for S3: 757 mn bbl of Hormuz crude to replace in 2027; SPR lasts 19 days unaided.
Contract 79% substitution so the SPR lasts 90 days; build an LPG reserve of 30 days (73% of LPG imports at risk under S3).
Even under reopening, 6% of crude imports stay exposed through 2027: keep SPR Phase-II on schedule.
MEA: Pursue assured-passage arrangements for Indian-flag and India-bound ships.
Lock in non-Gulf crude and LPG supply deals (Americas, West Africa, Russia) for 2027.
Coordinate the Red Sea route: Gulf bypass pipelines exit through Bab el-Mandeb.
DGS: Issue Gulf advisories tied to the Threat-Opacity Index; mandate GNSS-interference reporting.
NavIC-capable receivers on Indian-flag Gulf traders.
Brief masters on toll or inspection corridors and approved routes.
